exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: Strong scoring-engine work explains what every variable means — here is how one student built café loyalty points.

traits.trait: Defines each variable before using it
traits.sample: In my formula 4d + 2s, d is drinks bought and s is snacks — so 4d + 2s means 4 points per drink plus 2 per snack.
traits.why: Every letter is named in words, so the expression is readable.

traits.trait: Explains the distributive property in words
traits.sample: Double-points day turns 3(4d + 2s) into 12d + 6s: the 3 multiplies BOTH terms inside the parentheses.
traits.why: It says what happened to each term, not just the rewritten answer.

traits.sample: A streak bonus of 2⁴ = 16 points doubles four times — I chose an exponent because doubling repeats.
traits.why: The exponent is connected to repeated multiplication, not used decoratively.

traits.trait: Tests the formula with real numbers
traits.sample: For 2 drinks and 3 snacks: 4(2) + 2(3) = 14 points — substituting proved my expression works before I published it.
traits.why: Evaluating the expression is the evidence the model is correct.
